To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fluorine-containing amino acids can be incorporated in peptides to increase the proteolytic stability in human blood plasma and that this effect depends on the position and number of fluorine atoms in the amino acid.
fluorinated peptides show a reduced degradation by human plasma proteases, compared to the non-fluorinated peptide.
“The stability of peptides in blood plasma is increased when non-natural fluorinated amino acids are introduced into the peptide sequence.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new peptide based drugs and the improvement of the existing ones by the use of fluorinated non-natural amino acid building blocks.
the design and synthesis of a series of peptides containing non-natural amino acid residues, with the aim of improving proteolytic stability in human blood plasma.
the design, synthesis and enzymatic degradation of peptides containing non-natural fluorinated amino acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fluorinated peptides show a reduced degradation in human blood compared to the control.
the fluorinated peptides are less stable in blood plasma than the non-fluorinated peptides.

fluorination of the side chain of an amino acid can significantly increase the stability of peptides against human proteases, especially when the amino acids are located in the middle of the sequence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fluorination of peptides in general increases the stability in human blood plasma, but not to the same extent in all peptides.
fluorination can improve the enzymatic stability in human plasma of peptides containing a single non-natural amino acid residue.
the fluorination of peptides in the side chains of non-natural residues has a positive effect on the proteolytic stability in human blood plasma.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of fluorinated amino acid residues in a peptide can increase its stability in human blood plasma, but that the degree of stability depends on the specific position of the fluorinated amino acid residue in the peptide.
fluorinated amino acids can be used in the design of peptides that exhibit improved stability in human plasma.
fluorinated amino acids can be used to increase enzymatic stability, and that the degree of fluorination can be used to tune the stability of peptides.
